notes:
Background: Lodestone QueryGrid is a mid-market SaaS company providing KB-driven support automation for vertical B2B apps. They've built an ingest + vector pipeline in-house (FAISS) but are struggling at scale with cost and tail latency under heavy QPS. Interested in Redwood hosted API to accelerate time-to-value and offload serving ops.

Key ask summary (verbatim/near-verbatim from AE & engineering calls):
- 'We need to serve ~600-1000 QPS for chat/search assistants during peak windows; average query is small (10-40 tokens) but many concurrent sessions.'
- 'Index will be ~1.8M to 2.5M short documents (KB pages, Q&A pairs, product snippets).'
- 'We want p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms end-to-end for reranked responses; cost target ~<$0.005/query (embeddings + rerank + gen).'

Technical details discussed:
- Embedding strategy: customer currently uses 1536-d vectors (open model). Considering switching to a distilled open embedding to reduce index size and cost. Wants Redwood Optimize recommendations on quantization and embedding dimensionality tradeoffs.
- Reranking: prefers a lightweight bi-encoder for recall and a cross-encoder for top-20 rerank in critical flows. Concerned about cross-encoder latency at high QPS; asked about Redwood's batching / async reranker options and fallback to cheaper models.
- Index scale: 2M docs -> planning shard strategy, checkpointing, incremental indexing. Wants advice on hot segments and caching prefixes for heavy queries.
- Throughput/latency: target sustained ~800QPS with bursts to 1k QPS. Current in-house p99 ~650ms under 500 QPS; unacceptable.
- Cost sensitivity: looking to reduce per-query unit costs by 40-60% relative to current self-hosted infra.

Recent timeline (short bullets):
- 2026-02-18: Intro + product fit call (Fireflies ff-2026-02-18-lodestone-kickoff). AE Maya + SE Liam. Customer shared latency/cost baselines.
- 2026-02-24: Security questionnaire submitted (drive:/security/lodestone-security-answers-2026-03.pdf). Asking about data residency and KMS.
- 2026-03-05: Perf criteria workshop, Redwood provided preliminary qps/latency model (ff-2026-03-05-perf-review).
- 2026-03-09: Agreement on 7-day hosted API POC scope; SE to provide synthetic load script and perf checklist.

POC scope & acceptance criteria (agreed in call):
- Index a 2M-document export (customer will provide a 10% sample for initial run).
- Run steady-state 600 QPS for 30 minutes, then 1k QPS bursts for 2x 5-minute windows.
- Measure end-to-end p95/p99 for retrieval + rerank + final generation; p95 <= 150ms target, p99 < 300ms ideal.
- Track cost per query and token distribution; customer target <$0.005/query for search+rerank (embeddings + lightweight gen).

Security/compliance notes:
- Must support SAML SSO for admin console and audit logging on query-level events for compliance audits.
- EU data residency: at least one replica for EU customers (many of Lodestone's customers are in EU).
- KMS integration required for any persistent caches or index snapshots.

Decision influencers & internal champions:
- CTO Emma Rowland (technical owner) — cares most about tail latency and operational simplicity.
- Head of Product Mike Flores — cares about UX and relevance (rerank quality).

Open questions / blockers for Redwood sales/SE:
- Confirm p99 viability running cross-encoder reranker at target QPS with Redwood batching/fallback strategies.
- Provide concrete cost model showing break-even vs their current FAISS infra (include EP/embedding dims, quantization options).
- Legal/data residency: draft SOW language for EU residency + KMS handling.

Suggested next actions (AE/SE):
- SE Liam to hand over hosted API perf runbook + synthetic load script by 2026-03-12 (in progress).
- Schedule on-site (virtual) deep-dive with Lodestone infra team to walk through sample index and query distribution (proposed 2026-03-15).
- Prepare an ROI slide comparing self-hosted TCO vs Redwood hosted API with quantization recommendations (drive link placeholder).

- Mid-term: If POC meets goals, 12-month reserved capacity conversation for Dedicated or committed Hosted plan (estimated ARR range above).
